skill.name: agent-wallet
skill.description: Use ChainGPT agent-wallet instructions to manage a local EVM agent wallet with encrypted keystore storage, policy-gated signing, spend limits, and a localhost admin dashboard.
skill.summary: Manage a policy-gated local crypto wallet for an AI agent.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most shell-execution alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, not executable Ruby or shell code. The skill still has high-impact wallet behavior: local keystore and policy files, transaction signing, a localhost admin dashboard, and passphrase export guidance. Publish only with strong warnings and after the author removes risky secret-exposure guidance and reconciles unsupported-feature claims.

remediation.issue: Passphrase export guidance can print a wallet secret to the terminal.
remediation.suggestion: Remove inline secret-export commands from the skill text and direct users to an out-of-band backup procedure outside agent context.

remediation.issue: The wallet signing flow can move real crypto assets.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit human confirmation, transaction previews, conservative default caps, and clear warnings before any signing or broadcasting action.

remediation.issue: The local dashboard can edit wallet policy and toggle the kill switch.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the dashboard disabled by default, preserve loopback-only binding, enforce short-lived tokens, and document token handling requirements.

remediation.issue: Hidden keystore, policy, and admin-token files hold sensitive wallet control state.
remediation.suggestion: Document required file permissions, validate them at startup, and refuse operation if sensitive files are group-readable or world-readable.

remediation.issue: Solana and ERC-4337 support claims conflict with the limitations section.
remediation.suggestion: Reconcile the documentation so unsupported, beta, and implemented signing surfaces are clearly separated.

semantic_findings.title: Agent Wallet Can Sign and Broadcast Transactions
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents a signing tool as the only tool that can move funds and shows a pre-flight flow ending in transaction signing. Policy gates reduce risk, but the intended capability can transfer real crypto assets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document explicitly states the signing tool signs and broadcasts transactions and can move funds. The cited pre-flight checklist shows it as the final operational step.

semantic_findings.title: Local Dashboard Can Modify Wallet Policy
semantic_findings.description: The dashboard is described as authenticated and localhost-only, but it can edit the policy JSON and toggle the kill switch. A compromised token or local session could weaken or disable wallet guardrails.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file states the dashboard returns an admin token, includes a policy editor, and exposes POST routes for policy and kill-switch changes. These are clear administrative mutation paths.

semantic_findings.title: Contradictory Support Claims for Solana and ERC-4337
semantic_findings.description: The document presents Solana and ERC-4337 workflows, then later says non-EVM signing and session keys are not supported or are future features. This can mislead users about which signing surfaces are implemented and safe to use.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The same file contains detailed Solana and ERC-4337 sections and a later limitation section that denies those capabilities. The conflict is directly visible in the cited ranges.

content.value_statement: AI agents can move funds without clear operational boundaries. This skill documents a local wallet with policy-gated signing, spend caps, and admin controls.
actual_capabilities: Guides initialization of a ChainGPT agent EVM wallet with an encrypted local keystore.
Shows wallet address, policy digest, kill-switch state, and native balances through documented tools.
Describes policy-gated transaction signing and broadcasting through the agent wallet signing tool.
Documents allowlists, blocked addresses, spend caps, gas caps, selector blocks, and memo requirements.
Documents a localhost dashboard for status viewing, policy editing, kill switch control, and balance checks.
limitations: The reviewed package contains only SKILL.md, so implementation claims are not independently verifiable here.
The wallet can sign transactions that move real funds when policy permits.
Passphrase recovery is impossible if the backup is lost.
Solana and ERC-4337 support is described inconsistently in the same document.

output: The response names the exact policy rule that refused the transaction.
It recommends admin policy review instead of trying to bypass the rule.

best_practices: Start with the kill switch enabled until an admin reviews every policy limit.
Fund the wallet with small balances that match the policy caps and intended task.
Keep passphrases and dashboard tokens outside prompts, chat logs, and shared notes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the agent to work around a policy refusal.
Do not store wallet passphrases in prompts, shared notes, or command histories.
Do not expose the dashboard beyond localhost or leave it running unattended.

faq.question: Does this skill custody funds?
faq.answer: No. The document describes custody on the user machine through local keystore files.

faq.question: Can the agent change its policy?
faq.answer: The skill says MCP tools cannot write the policy. The local dashboard can edit it after admin authentication.

faq.question: Can it move real crypto assets?
faq.answer: Yes. The signing flow can broadcast transactions that move funds when policy permits.

faq.question: Is Solana supported?
faq.answer: The document contains conflicting statements. Treat Solana support as unverified until the author reconciles the documentation.

faq.question: What happens if the passphrase is lost?
faq.answer: The keystore cannot be recovered without the passphrase. Users must keep an offline backup.

faq.question: Is it suitable for automatic installation?
faq.answer: No. It handles wallet keys, local files, a dashboard, and transactions, so it needs explicit review.
